title: Release Highlights Schema
description: The short, user-facing summary of one release, in releases/<version>.yaml. `paramify update` shows it instead of the CHANGELOG, which is written for maintainers and runs to thousands of lines. A release without a file still updates; the command points at its CHANGELOG section instead. See releases/README.md.

version.description: The release, as its CHANGELOG heading writes it and without the tag's leading v (0.6.0-beta for tag v0.6.0-beta). Must equal the file's basename.

date.description: Release date. Optional: the CHANGELOG heading's date is used when this is absent.

highlights.description: Three to five rows of what is new, plus one `breaking` row per Breaking entry in the CHANGELOG. The 3-5 limit on the other rows is checked by tests/test_release_highlights.py, not here, so the message can say which rows to cut.

tag.description: The pill shown before the title. `breaking` rows are listed apart from the rest, before the confirm prompt, with their `fix`.

title.description: One line a user understands without the CHANGELOG. Say what they get or must do, not how it was built.

detail.description: Optional second line, shown dimmed under the title.

try.description: Optional command to try the change, shown in the closing panel. Must be a paramify command.

fix.description: What the user does about a breaking change. Required on `breaking` rows.

fetchers.description: Fetcher names the change affects. Shell-style globs work (okta_*). A breaking row with fetchers names each of the user's manifests that uses one; a fetcher row moves to the top when the user runs it.
